title: Nashville employees reportedly edited WatchGuard body-camera footage without permission
summary: WPLN reported that a Metro Nashville Police Department internal investigation found two civilian IT employees had removed profanity from body-camera recordings without permission, including footage supplied to the Community Oversight Board for a police-misconduct investigation. WPLN later reported that MNPD was reviewing more than 300 recordings, but the underlying internal-investigation file is not linked in a stable public copy and the available reports are from one newsroom.

sources.title: Internal investigation shows editing of MNPD body camera footage was more widespread than claimed
key_claims: WPLN reported that an obtained internal investigation found two IT employees edited body-camera footage without permission.
WPLN reported that edited footage had been supplied to the Community Oversight Board during a police-misconduct investigation.

sources.title: More than 300 body camera videos are under review by MNPD for improper editing
key_claims: WPLN reported that MNPD was reviewing more than 300 recordings for improper editing.

verification_status.reason: The reports quote and describe an MNPD internal investigation, but the underlying record is not linked in a stable public copy and all available detailed reporting located so far comes from one newsroom.
evidence_needed: A stable copy of the MNPD internal-investigation record or audit findings
Independent reliable corroboration of the unauthorized editing and its scope

title: Tesla employees reportedly shared sensitive vehicle-camera recordings
summary: Reuters reported, based on interviews with nine former employees, that Tesla workers circulated sensitive images and videos captured by customer-vehicle cameras through internal messaging channels between 2019 and 2022. A later proposed class action repeated the allegations, and two U.S. senators requested answers from Tesla. No public regulator finding, adjudicated merits finding, or company admission has been located, so the case remains reported but unverified.

sources.title: Tesla hit with class action lawsuit over alleged privacy intrusion
key_claims: Reuters reported that nine former employees described internal sharing of sensitive customer-camera recordings between 2019 and 2022.

sources.title: Yeh v. Tesla class-action complaint
sources.publisher: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California
key_claims: The complaint alleged that Tesla employees accessed and shared invasive customer-camera recordings for personal entertainment.

sources.title: Letter to Tesla on Vehicle Camera Recordings
sources.publisher: U.S. Senators Edward Markey and Richard Blumenthal
key_claims: The senators requested information from Tesla about employee access, internal sharing, safeguards, and customer notice.

verification_status.reason: Detailed allegations come from former-employee reporting and a civil complaint, neither of which is an adjudicated finding. No regulator finding or Tesla admission has been located.
evidence_needed: A public regulator or law-enforcement finding substantiating employee sharing
A Tesla admission, audit record, or adjudicated court finding on the alleged conduct

title: Cypress men reportedly detained after deputies followed the wrong Flock-flagged car
summary: ABC13 reported that Harris County deputies detained two 19-year-old men at gunpoint on August 3, 2023 after a Flock alert identified a stolen Chevrolet Camaro and an undercover unit followed a similar car without confirming its plate. Deputies released the men after determining they had stopped the wrong vehicle. No incident report, department finding, lawsuit, or independent contemporaneous report has been located.

sources.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
key_claims: ABC13 reported that deputies detained two men after following a similar Camaro without confirming it matched the plate in a Flock stolen-vehicle alert.

verification_status.reason: The incident is supported by one contemporaneous local-news report. Later indexes repeat that account rather than independently corroborating it, and no underlying department or court record has been located.
evidence_needed: The Harris County Sheriff's Office incident report, dispatch record, or internal review
A direct copy of the Flock alert and records identifying where the vehicle match failed
Independent contemporaneous reporting or a court filing from the detained men

title: Texas sheriff's office reportedly used national Flock search in abortion-related investigation
summary: 404 Media reported that the Johnson County Sheriff's Office searched a nationwide Flock camera network for a woman who had self-administered an abortion. The same newsroom later reported that court records characterized the matter as a death investigation and showed investigators considered possible criminal charges.

sources.title: A Texas Cop Searched License Plate Cameras Nationwide for a Woman Who Got an Abortion
key_claims: 404 Media reported that the sheriff's office searched a nationwide Flock camera network for the woman.

sources.title: Police Said They Surveilled Woman Who Had an Abortion for Her 'Safety.' Court Records Show They Considered Charging Her With a Crime
key_claims: The follow-up said court records described a death investigation and possible criminal charges.

verification_status.reason: Both available reports come from the same newsroom, and the underlying court record is not linked in a stable public copy.
evidence_needed: The underlying court record or another primary official record
Independent reliable corroboration of the Flock search and its purpose

title: Burbank audit reportedly found former employees retained Flock access
summary: Public Records Southern California reported that a Burbank Police Department audit, signed May 15, 2026, recorded the deactivation of three recently separated employees' Flock accounts. The report links the audit produced through a California public-records request, but no independent newsroom or direct city finding has established how long the accounts remained usable or whether any former employee accessed the system.

sources.title: Burbank Built a Surveillance Network And Nobody Was Watching.
key_claims: The report says a May 2026 department audit recorded the deactivation of three recently separated employees' Flock accounts.

verification_status.reason: The claim currently rests on one advocacy publisher's interpretation of records it obtained. The linked audit does not establish how long the accounts remained active or whether the former employees used them after leaving.
evidence_needed: A stable direct copy of the complete audit production from the City of Burbank
Account or access logs establishing whether the former employees logged in after separation
An official city response or independent reliable corroboration

title: Goodyear officer reportedly investigated for suspected Flock misuse
summary: ABC15 Arizona reported that a July 2026 Goodyear Police Department audit identified concerning Flock activity and that one officer was placed on leave pending a criminal investigation handled by another agency. The department's underlying audit, press release, officer identity, searches, and alleged purpose have not been located in a stable public record, so the suspected misuse remains unverified.

sources.title: Goodyear Police Dept. investigate whether officer misused Flock license plate reader system
key_claims: ABC15 reported that a July audit raised concerns and one officer was placed on leave pending a criminal investigation.

verification_status.reason: Only one news report has been located, and the department's referenced press release and audit are not available in a stable public copy. The report does not identify the officer, searches, alleged target, or purpose.
evidence_needed: The Goodyear Police Department press release and underlying July 2026 Flock audit
A charging record, investigative finding, or official case disposition
Independent reliable reporting that identifies the suspected searches and their purpose

title: Raleigh audits reportedly listed former employees as active Flock users
summary: A Raleigh community post, citing audit files released through MuckRock, reported that an April 8, 2026 Raleigh Police Department audit found several active Flock users were no longer department employees. The post further alleged the condition remained unresolved in a May audit. The underlying public-record production is linked, but the claim has not been independently reported and the affected accounts have not been publicly identified.

sources.title: Raleigh Police appears to have ignored their own audits
key_claims: The post quotes an April 2026 audit as saying several active Flock users were no longer employed by the department.

sources.title: Flock Safety ALPR data request — Raleigh Police Department
key_claims: The request page is the cited repository for the Raleigh Police Department audit files discussed in the community post.

verification_status.reason: The allegation is explained only in a community post. Although that post points to a public-record production, no independent report or official response has verified the interpretation or whether access persisted.
evidence_needed: Stable direct links to the April 8 and May 5, 2026 audit documents
Raleigh Police confirmation of the number and status of former-employee accounts
Access logs showing whether any former employee used an account after separation
